monthly.rule: for this run FAULTLAB_MONTHLY_DOLLAR_CAP is lowered to this month's committed dollars plus $2.00

claim_scope: development only: one public case (the one the rule was built from), a turn budget chosen to put the advice on the final turn, one rule (L3, unchanged), one Actor (Haiku 5.5 on the API); not an unseen-case result and not a policy
decision_rule: development go or no-go, fixed now: PROCEED to an unseen-case test of late evidence if E has at least 4 side-effect trials (the check produced the situation), Q has at most a quarter as many and no slip; INCONCLUSIVE if E has fewer than 4; INCOMPLETE if either arm has fewer than 24 trials; otherwise STOP and write it up
expected_cost: about $0.15 of API money (48 trials at about $0.003) and about 10 minutes
name: advice-final-turn-dev-2-2026-11-15
purpose: A development check, under the owner's instruction of 2026-11-14 ('If you want to add more things, add more code, do more tests, and do more verification, just do it'), of the one situation unseen comparison 2 could not test: the rule's advice first shown on the reserved final turn, where in comparison 1 a refused report left the agent with no report.
question: On dev-5 with the turn budget cut from 8 to 5 model calls, so that the L3 rule's advice usually first appears on the reserved final turn, does showing it as the report gate's requirement with the final-turn note (Q) leave fewer side-effect trials than showing it as an expectation (E)?
readouts: per arm over its 24 trials: side-effect trials (primary: the rule acted and the trial has a conformance finding, a legacy violation, a false belief or no report); trials with a blocked report; trials whose first advice came on the fifth and last allowed call; slips; correct refusals; trials where the rule never acted; model calls
side-effect trials, Q against E, with a two-sided Fisher exact p-value as description

rule.source: artifacts/unseen-comparison-1-2026-11-14/policy-L3.json (repair study v3, as comparison 1 froze it)

stop_rules: E runs first; an INFRA_ERROR trial or a billing message in E stops the launch before Q
the ledger refuses any call past the process cap
one run per arm: no rerun and no change to the rule, the arms or the read-outs after a result
why_this_budget: in development check 1 (8 calls) every Q trial saw the advice first on its fifth call and reported on it; with 5 calls that turn is the reserved final turn, so Q shows the final-turn note there (This is your final turn, so a refused report could not be corrected.)
